_comment: Machine-readable provenance for the 60-item pilot. src/validate.load_annotations reads THIS file, not provenance.md, which is the human-readable record. Fields already filled are facts about the draw and the instrument, verifiable from the repository. Fields set to null or 'TO BE COMPLETED' are human declarations: validate_annotation_provenance rejects this file until a person replaces every one of them, and it is meant to be rejected until then.
annotator_role: TO BE COMPLETED - a role, never a name. e.g. 'project analyst'
_label_source: Set to "human" only if a person produced every label. Any other value fails validation, which is the point.
_blind_to_model_outputs: true only if you did not consult any model output while labelling. Scores exist in interim/scores.parquet from 2026-09-10, so this asserts you did not open the cache - not merely that nothing was shown to you.
_independent_of_analyst: true if the annotator is not the person running the analysis. If the analyst labelled it, this is false, and the report states that limitation rather than hiding it.
_scores_existed: true if model scores existed anywhere at labelling time. As of 2026-09-10 the full pass is complete, so this is true. Validation protocol section 5 permits labelling after scoring provided the cache is not consulted, and requires recording which case obtained.
_sessions: One entry per sitting: {"start": "2026-09-10T14:00:00Z", "end": "2026-09-10T14:35:00Z"}. Timestamps need a time zone. Record when it actually happened; an empty list fails validation.
_deviations: Every rubric question that arose and how it was resolved, as strings. An empty list means none arose - do not leave it empty to save effort, because section 6 reads it as evidence about rubric adequacy.
_superseded: Superseded 2026-09-10 by provenance_v2.json. This template was written for rubric v1; v1 labels live in pilot_manual_annotations.csv and are retained as the rubric-assessment evidence that produced v2, not as study labels.
